context.title: From Adam to Edom
context.summary: The book opens with a family tree running from Adam through Noah's sons to Abraham, Isaac and Esau, ending with the kings and chiefs of Edom.
context.background: This chapter compresses the genealogies of Genesis 5, 10, 11, 25 and 36 into a few lines. Starting with Adam places Israel's story inside the story of all humanity. Ancient genealogies could skip generations and sometimes list peoples or places as 'sons' — Mizraim, for example, is the Hebrew name for Egypt.

customs.note: 'Duke' is the KJV's word for a clan chief, not a European noble title.

watchFor: A pattern repeats: side branches (Japheth, Ham, Ishmael, Esau) are listed first, then the chosen line continues.
The brief note about Peleg, 'in his days the earth was divided' (v. 19).

people.name: Adam
people.summary: Red, a Babylonian word, the generic name for man, having the same meaning in the Hebrew and the Assyrian languages. It was the name given to the first man, whose creation, fall, and subsequent history and that of his descendants are detailed in the first book of Moses (Gen. 1:27-ch. 5).

people.name: Seth
people.summary: Appointed; a substitute, the third son of Adam and Eve (Gen. 4:25; 5:3).

people.name: Enos
people.summary: Man the son of Seth, and grandson of Adam (Gen. 5:6-11; Luke 3:38). He lived nine hundred and five years.

people.name: Cainan
people.summary: The fourth antediluvian patriarch, the eldest son of Enos. He was 70 years old at the birth of his eldest son Mahalaleel, after which he lived 840 years (Gen. 5:9-14), and was 910 years old when he died.

people.name: Jared
people.summary: The fourth antediluvian patriarch in descent from Seth (Gen. 5:15-20; Luke 3:37), the father of Enoch; called Jered in 1 Chr. 1:2.

people.name: Mahalaleel
people.summary: The son of Cainan, of the line of Seth (Gen. 5:12-17); called Maleleel (Luke 3:37).

people.name: Enoch
people.summary: The son of Jared, and father of Methuselah (Gen. 5:21; Luke 3:37). His father was one hundred and sixty-two years old when he was born. After the birth of Methuselah, Enoch “walked with God three hundred years” (Gen. 5:22-24), when he was translated without tasting death.

people.name: Lamech
people.summary: The seventh in descent from Seth, being the only son of Methuselah.

people.name: Methuselah
people.summary: Man of the dart, the son of Enoch, and grandfather of Noah.

people.name: Noah
people.summary: Rest, (Heb. Noah) the grandson of Methuselah (Gen. 5:25-29), who was for two hundred and fifty years contemporary with Adam, and the son of Lamech, who was about fifty years old at the time of Adam’s death.

people.name: Shem
people.summary: A name; renown, the first mentioned of the sons of Noah (Gen. 5:32; 6:10). He was probably the eldest of Noah’s sons. The words “brother of Japheth the elder” in Gen. 10:21 are more correctly rendered “the elder brother of Japheth,” as in the Revised Version.

people.name: Ham
people.summary: Warm, hot, and hence the south; also an Egyptian word meaning “black”, the youngest son of Noah (Gen. 5:32; comp. 9:22, 24).

people.name: Japheth
people.summary: Wide spreading: “God shall enlarge Japheth” (Heb. Yaphat Elohim le-Yephet, Gen. 9:27. Some, however, derive the name from yaphah, “to be beautiful;” hence white), one of the sons of Noah, mentioned last in order (Gen. 5:32; 6:10; 7:13), perhaps first by birth (10:21; comp. 9:24).

people.name: Tubal
people.summary: The fifth son of Japheth (Gen. 10:2).

people.name: Javan
people.summary: The fourth “son” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), whose descendants settled in Greece, i.e., Ionia, which bears the name of Javan in Hebrew. Alexander the Great is called the “king of Javan” (rendered “Grecia,” Dan. 8:21; 10:20; comp. 11:2; Zech. 9:13).

people.name: Meshech
people.summary: Drawing out, the sixth son of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), the founder of a tribe (1 Chr. 1:5; Ezek. 27:13; 38:2, 3). They were in all probability the Moschi, a people inhabiting the Moschian Mountains, between the Black and the Caspian Seas.

people.name: Gomer
people.summary: The eldest son of Japheth, and father of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah (Gen. 10:2, 3), whose descendants formed the principal branch of the population of South-eastern Europe.

people.name: Magog
people.summary: Region of Gog, the second of the “sons” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2; 1 Chr. 1:5). In Ezekiel (38:2; 39:6) it is the name of a nation, probably some Scythian or Tartar tribe descended from Japheth.

people.name: Madai
people.summary: Middle land, the third “son” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), the name by which the Medes are known on the Assyrian monuments.

people.name: Tiras
people.summary: The youngest of the sons of Japheth (Gen. 10:2; 1 Chr. 1:5).

people.name: Togarmah
people.summary: A son of Gomer, and grandson of Japheth (Gen. 10:3).

people.name: Ashkenaz
people.summary: One of the three sons of Gomer (Gen. 10:3), and founder of one of the tribes of the Japhetic race.

people.name: Riphath
people.summary: A crusher, Gomer’s second son (Gen. 10:3), supposed to have been the ancestor of the Paphlagonians.

people.name: Dodanim
people.summary: Leaders, a race descended from Javan (Gen. 10:4). They are known in profane history as the Dardani, originally inhabiting Illyricum. They were a semi-Pelasgic race, and in the ethnographical table (Gen. 10) they are grouped with the Chittim.

people.name: Elishah
people.summary: The oldest of the four sons of Javan (Gen. 10:4), whose descendants peopled Greece. It has been supposed that Elishah’s descendants peopled the Peloponnesus, which was known by the name of Elis.

people.name: Tarshish
people.summary: One of the “sons” of Javan (Gen. 10:4; 1 Chr. 1:7).

people.name: Canaan
people.summary: The fourth son of Ham (Gen. 10:6). His descendants were under a curse in consequence of the transgression of his father (9:22-27). His eldest son, Zidon, was the father of the Sidonians and Phoenicians.

people.name: Cush
people.summary: A son, probably the eldest, of Ham, and the father of Nimrod (Gen. 10:8; 1 Chr. 1:10). From him the land of Cush seems to have derived its name.

people.name: Mizraim
people.summary: The dual form of matzor, meaning a “mound” or “fortress,” the name of a people descended from Ham (Gen. 10:6, 13; 1 Chr. 1:8, 11). It was the name generally given by the Hebrews to the land of Egypt, and may denote the two Egypts, the Upper and the Lower.

people.name: Phut
people.summary: One of the sons of Ham (Gen. 10:6).

people.name: Dedan
people.summary: A son of Raamah (Gen. 10:7). His descendants are mentioned in Isa. 21:13, and Ezek. 27:15.

people.name: Havilah
people.summary: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

people.name: Raamah
people.summary: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

people.name: Sabtah
people.summary: Rest, the third son of Cush (Gen. 10:7; 1 Chr. 1:9).

people.name: Sabtecha
people.summary: The fifth son of Cush.

people.name: Seba
people.summary: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

people.name: Sheba
people.summary: Heb. shebha, the son of Raamah (Gen. 10:7), whose descendants settled with those of Dedan on the Persian Gulf.

people.name: Nimrod
people.summary: Firm, a descendant of Cush, the son of Ham. He was the first who claimed to be a “mighty one in the earth.” Babel was the beginning of his kingdom, which he gradually enlarged (Gen. 10:8-10).

people.name: Anamim
people.summary: The name of an Egyptian tribe descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:13; 1 Chr. 1:11).

people.name: Ludim
people.summary: Probably the same as Lud (2) (comp. Gen. 10:13; 1 Chr. 1:11).

people.name: Naphtuhim
people.summary: A Hamitic tribe descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:13). Others identify this word with Napata, the name of the city and territory on the southern frontier of Mizraim, the modern Meroe, at the great bend of the Nile at Soudan.

people.name: Casluhim
people.summary: Fortified, a people descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:14; 1 Chr. 1:12).

people.name: Heth
people.summary: Dread, a descendant of Canaan, and the ancestor of the Hittites (Gen. 10:18; Deut. 7:1), who dwelt in the vicinity of Hebron (Gen. 23:3, 7).

people.name: Zidon
people.summary: A fishery, a town on the Mediterranean coast, about 25 miles north of Tyre. It received its name from the “first-born” of Canaan, the grandson of Noah (Gen. 10:15, 19).

people.name: Amorite
people.summary: Highlanders, or hillmen, the name given to the descendants of one of the sons of Canaan (Gen. 14:7), called Amurra or Amurri in the Assyrian and Egyptian inscriptions.

people.name: Girgasite
people.summary: Dwelling in clayey soil, the descendants of the fifth son of Canaan (Gen. 10:16), one of the original tribes inhabiting the land of Canaan before the time of the Israelites (Gen. 15:21; Deut. 7:1).

people.name: Jebusite
people.summary: The name of the original inhabitants of Jebus, mentioned frequently among the seven nations doomed to destruction (Gen. 10:16; 15:21; Ex. 3:8, 17; 13:5, etc.).

people.name: Hivite
people.summary: One of the original tribes scattered over Palestine, from Hermon to Gibeon in the south. The name is interpreted as “midlanders” or “villagers” (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15).

people.name: Arkite
people.summary: (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15), a designation of certain descendants from the Phoenicians or Sidonians, the inhabitants of Arka, 12 miles north of Tripoli, opposite the northern extremity of Lebanon.

people.name: Sinite
people.summary: An inhabitant of Sin, near Arka (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15).

people.name: Zemarite
people.summary: The designation of one of the Phoenician tribes (Gen. 10:18) who inhabited the town of Sumra, at the western base of the Lebanon range.

people.name: Arphaxad
people.summary: Son of Shem, born the year after the Deluge. He died at the age of 438 years (Gen. 11:10-13; 1 Chr. 1:17, 18; Luke 3:36). He dwelt in Mesopotamia, and became, according to the Jewish historian Josephus, the progenitor of the Chaldeans.

people.name: Asshur
people.summary: Second son of Shem (Gen. 10:22; 1 Chr. 1:17). He went from the land of Shinar and built Nineveh, etc. (Gen. 10:11, 12). He probably gave his name to Assyria, which is the usual translation of the word, although the form Asshur is sometimes retained (Num. 24:22, 24; Ezek. 27:23, etc.).

people.name: Aram
people.summary: The son of Shem (Gen. 10:22); according to Gen. 22:21, a grandson of Nahor.

people.name: Elam
people.summary: Highland, the son of Shem (Gen. 10:22), and the name of the country inhabited by his descendants (14:1, 9; Isa. 11:11; 21:2, etc.) lying to the east of Babylonia, and extending to the shore of the Mediterranean, a distance in a direct line of about 1,000 miles.

people.name: Hul
people.summary: Circle, the second son of Aram (Gen. 10:23), and grandson of Shem.

people.name: Lud
people.summary: The fourth son of Shem (Gen. 10:22; 1 Chr. 1:17), ancestor of the Lydians probably.

people.name: Mash
people.summary: (= Meshech 1 Chr. 1:17), one of the four sons of Aram, and the name of a tribe descended from him (Gen. 10:23) inhabiting some part probably of Mesopotamia.

people.name: Uz
people.summary: The son of Aram, and grandson of Shem (Gen. 10:23; 1 Chr. 1:17).

people.name: Eber
people.summary: The third post-duluvian patriach after Shem (Gen. 10:24; 11:14). He is regarded as the founder of the Hebrew race (10:21; Num. 24:24).

people.name: Salah
people.summary: A shoot, a descendant of Arphaxed (Luke 3:35, 36); called also Shelah (1 Chr. 1:18, 24).

people.name: Peleg
people.summary: Division, one of the sons of Eber; so called because “in his days was the earth divided” (Gen. 10:25). Possibly he may have lived at the time of the dispersion from Babel.

people.name: Joktan
people.summary: Little, the second of the two sons of Eber (Gen. 10:25; 1 Chr. 1:19). There is an Arab tradition that Joktan (Arab.

people.name: Almodad
people.summary: Immeasurable, the first named of the sons of Joktan (Gen. 10:26), the founder of an Arabian tribe.

people.name: Hazarmaveth
people.summary: Court of death, the third son of Joktan, and a region in Arabia-Felix settled by him (Gen. 10:26; 1 Chr. 1:20).

people.name: Hadoram
people.summary: The fifth son of Joktan, the founder of an Arab tribe (Gen. 10:27; 1 Chr. 1:21).

people.name: Uzal
people.summary: A wanderer, a descendant of Joktan (Gen. 10:27; 1 Chr. 1:21), the founder apparently of one of the Arab tribes; the name also probably of the province they occupied and of their chief city.

people.name: Abimael
people.summary: Father of Mael, one of the sons or descendants of Joktan, in Northern Arabia (Gen. 10:28; 1 Chr. 1:22).

people.name: Ebal
people.summary: A descendant of Eber (1 Chr. 1:22), called also Obal (Gen. 10:28).

people.name: Sheba
people.summary: Heb. id.

people.name: Havilah
people.summary: A son of Joktan (Gen. 10:29; 1 Chr. 1:23).

people.name: Jobab
people.summary: One of the sons of Joktan, and founder of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 10:29).

people.name: Ophir
people.summary: One of the sons of Joktan (Gen. 10:29).

people.name: Terah
people.summary: The wanderer; loiterer, for some unknown reason emigrated with his family from his native mountains in the north to the plains of Mesopotamia.

people.name: Nahor
people.summary: The father of Terah, who was the father of Abraham (Gen. 11:22-25; Luke 3:34).

people.name: Serug
people.summary: Branch, the father of Nahor (Gen. 11:20-23); called Saruch in Luke 3:35.

people.name: Abraham
people.summary: Father of a multitude, son of Terah, named (Gen. 11:27) before his older brothers Nahor and Haran, because he was the heir of the promises. Till the age of seventy, Abram sojourned among his kindred in his native country of Chaldea.

people.name: Isaac
people.summary: The only son of Abraham by Sarah. He was the longest lived of the three patriarchs (Gen. 21:1-3).

people.name: Ishmael
people.summary: Abraham’s eldest son, by Hagar the concubine (Gen. 16:15; 17:23). He was born at Mamre, when Abraham was eighty-six years of age, eleven years after his arrival in Canaan (16:3; 21:5).

people.name: Kedar
people.summary: Dark-skinned, the second son of Ishmael (Gen. 25:13).

people.name: Nebajoth
people.summary: Ishmael’s eldest son (Gen. 25:13), and the prince of an Israelitish tribe (16).

people.name: Adbeel
people.summary: Miracle of God, the third of the twelve sons of Ishmael, and head of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:13; 1 Chr. 1:29).

people.name: Mibsam
people.summary: One of Ishmael’s twelve sons, and head of an Arab tribe (Gen. 25:13).

people.name: Hadar
people.summary: A son of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15); in 1 Chr. 1:30 written Hadad.

people.name: Massa
people.summary: A lifting up, gift, one of the sons of Ishmael, the founder of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:14); a nomad tribe inhabiting the Arabian desert toward Babylonia.

people.name: Mishma
people.summary: One of the sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:14), and founder of an Arab tribe.

people.name: Jetur
people.summary: An enclosure, one of the twelve sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15).

people.name: Kedemah
people.summary: Eastward, the last-named of the sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15).

people.name: Midian
people.summary: Strife, the fourth son of Abraham by Keturah, the father of the Midianites (Gen. 25:2; 1 Chr. 1:32).

people.name: Keturah
people.summary: Incense, the wife of Abraham, whom he married probably after Sarah’s death (Gen. 25:1-6), by whom he had six sons, whom he sent away into the east country.

people.name: Jokshan
people.summary: Snarer, the second son of Abraham and Keturah (Gen. 25:2, 3; 1 Chr. 1:32).

people.name: Dedan
people.summary: A son of Jokshan, Abraham’s son by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:32). His descendants settled on the Syrian borders about the territory of Edom.

people.name: Ishbak
people.summary: Leaving, one of Abraham’s sons by Keturah (Gen. 25:2).

people.name: Medan
people.summary: A son of Jokshan, Abraham’s son by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:32). His descendants settled on the Syrian borders about the territory of Edom.

people.name: Sheba
people.summary: Heb. id.

people.name: Shuah
people.summary: One of Abraham’s sons by Keturah (Gen. 25:2; Chr. 1:32).

people.name: Zimran
people.summary: Vine-dressers; celebrated, one of the sons of Abraham by Keturah (Gen. 25:2).

people.name: Ephah
people.summary: Descendant of Keturah.

people.name: Abida
people.summary: Or Abi’dah, father of knowledge; knowing, one of the five sons of Midian, who was the son of Abraham by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:33), and apparently the chief of an Arab tribe.

people.name: Epher
people.summary: One of the sons of Midian, who was Abraham’s son by Keturah (Gen. 25:4).

people.name: Esau
people.summary: Hairy, Rebekah’s first-born twin son (Gen. 25:25). The name of Edom, “red”, was also given to him from his conduct in connection with the red lentil “pottage” for which he sold his birthright (30, 31).

people.name: Eliphaz
people.summary: The son of Esau by his wife Adah, and father of several Edomitish tribes (Gen. 36:4, 10, 11, 16).

people.name: Reuel
people.summary: A son of Esau and Bashemath (Gen. 36:4, 10; 1 Chr. 1:35).

people.name: Jaalam
people.summary: Concealer, the second of Esau’s three sons by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:5, 14).

people.name: Jeush
people.summary: The oldest of Esau’s three sons by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:5, 14, 18).

people.name: Korah
people.summary: The third son of Esau, by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:14; 1 Chr. 1:35).

people.name: Amalek
people.summary: Dweller in a valley, the son of Eliphaz and grandson of Esau (Gen. 36:12; 1 Chr. 1:36); the chief of an Idumean tribe (Gen. 36:16).

people.name: Kenaz
people.summary: The sons of Eliphaz.

people.name: Omar
people.summary: Eloquent, the son of Eliphaz, who was Esau’s eldest son (Gen. 36:11-15).

people.name: Teman
people.summary: Son of Eliphaz.

people.name: Timna
people.summary: Lotan's sister.

people.name: Nahath
people.summary: One of the four sons of Reuel, the son of Esau (Gen. 36:13, 17).

people.name: Shammah
people.summary: One of the “dukes” of Edom (Gen. 36:13, 17).

people.name: Zerah
people.summary: Grandson of Esau’s wife Basemath.

people.name: Dishan
people.summary: Antelope, the youngest son of Seir the Horite, head of one of the tribes of Idumaea (Gen. 36:21, 28, 30).

people.name: Ezer
people.summary: One of the sons of Seir, the native princes, “dukes,” of Mount Hor (Gen. 36:21, 27).

people.name: Lotan
people.summary: Coverer, one of the sons of Seir, the Horite (Gen. 36:20, 29).

people.name: Shobal
people.summary: The second son of Seir the Horite; one of the Horite “dukes” (Gen. 36:20).

people.name: Dishon
people.summary: Duke of Horites.

people.name: Seir
people.summary: A Horite; one of the “dukes” of Edom (Gen. 36:20-30).

people.name: Lydia
people.summary: A woman of Thyatira, a “seller of purple,” who dwelt in Philippi (Acts 16:14, 15). She was not a Jewess but a proselyte. The Lord opened her heart as she heard the gospel from the lips of Paul (16:13).

people.name: Anah
people.summary: Discoverer of Hot Springs.

people.name: Ebal
people.summary: A descendant of Seir the Horite (Gen. 36:23).

people.name: Onam
people.summary: Sons of Shobal.

people.name: Akan
people.summary: He twists, one of the sons of Ezer, the son of Seir the Horite (1 Chr. 1:42).

people.name: Aran
people.summary: Wild goat, a descendant of Seir the Horite (Gen. 36:28).

people.name: Bilhan
people.summary: The sons of Ezer.

people.name: Uz
people.summary: One of the Horite “dukes” in the land of Edom (Gen. 36:28).

people.name: Zavan
people.summary: Terror, one of the “dukes of Edom” (Gen. 36:27); called also Zavan (1 Chr. 1:42).

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Bela
people.summary: The son of Beor, and a king of Edom (Gen. 36:32, 33; 1 Chr. 1:43).

people.name: Beor
people.summary: The father of Bela, one of the kings of Edom (Gen. 36:32).

people.name: Jobab
people.summary: King of Edom, succeeded Bela (Gen. 36:33, 34).

people.name: Zerah
people.summary: Of Bozrah.

people.name: Moab
people.summary: Used to denote the people of Moab (Num. 22:3-14; Judg. 3:30; 2 Sam. 8:2; Jer. 48:11, 13).

people.name: Hadad
people.summary: An Edomite king who defeated the Midianites (Gen. 36:35; 1 Chr. 1:46).

people.name: Shaul
people.summary: A king of Edom (Gen. 36:37, 38); called Shaul in 1 Chr. 1:48.

people.name: Baal-hanan
people.summary: A king of Edom, son of Achbor (Gen. 36:38, 39; 1 Chr. 1:49, 50).

people.name: Achbor
people.summary: An Edomitish king (Gen. 36:38; 1 Chr. 1:49).

people.name: Hadad
people.summary: One of the Edomitish kings (Gen. 36:39) about the time of Saul.

people.name: Mehetabel
people.summary: Wife of Hadad, one of the kings of Edom (Gen. 36:39).

people.name: Mezahab
people.summary: Water of gold, the father of Matred (Gen. 36:39; 1 Chr. 1:50), and grandfather of Mehetabel, wife of Hadar, the last king of Edom.

people.name: Jetheth
people.summary: A peg, or a prince, one of the Edomitish kings of Mount Seir (Gen. 36:40).

people.name: Timnah
people.summary: A “duke” or sheik of Edom (Gen. 36:40).

people.name: Aholibamah
people.summary: Edomite chief.

people.name: Elah
people.summary: One of the Edomite chiefs or “dukes” of Mount Seir (Gen. 36:41).

people.name: Kenaz
people.summary: Teman.

people.name: Mibzar
people.summary: Fortress, one of the Edomitish “dukes” descended from Esau (Gen. 36:42; 1 Chr. 1:53).

people.name: Teman
people.summary: A chief of Edom.

people.name: Iram
people.summary: Citizen, chief of an Edomite tribe in Mount Seir (Gen. 36:43).

places.name: Dinhabah
places.summary: Robbers’ den, an Edomitish city, the capital of king Bela (Gen. 36:32).

places.name: Edom
places.summary: Idumea (Isa. 34:5, 6; Ezek. 35:15). “The field of Edom” (Gen. 32:3), “the land of Edom” (Gen. 36:16), was mountainous (Obad. 1:8, 9, 19, 21).

places.name: Bozrah
places.summary: The city of Jobab, one of the early Edomite kings (Gen. 36:33). This place is mentioned by the prophets in later times (Isa. 34:6; Jer. 49:13; Amos 1:12; Micah 2:12).

places.name: Midian
places.summary: An Arabian tribe descended from Midian. They inhabited principally the desert north of the peninsula of Arabia. The peninsula of Sinai was the pasture-ground for their flocks.

places.name: Moab
places.summary: The land of Moab (Jer. 48:24), called also the “country of Moab” (Ruth 1:2, 6; 2:6), on the east of Jordan and the Dead Sea, and south of the Arnon (Num. 21:13, 26).

places.name: Masrekah
places.summary: Vineyard of noble vines, a place in Idumea, the native place of Samlah, one of the Edomitish kings (Gen. 36:36; 1 Chr. 1:47).

places.name: Euphrates
places.summary: Hebrew, Perath; Assyrian, Purat; Persian cuneiform, Ufratush, whence Greek Euphrates, meaning “sweet water.” The Assyrian name means “the stream,” or “the great stream.”

places.name: Rehoboth
places.summary: An ancient city on the Euphrates (Gen. 36:37; 1 Chr. 1:48), “Rehoboth by the river.”

events.title: Birth of Enos
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 4:26 – 1 Chronicles 1:1. People: Enos, Seth.

events.title: Birth of Seth
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 4:25 – Luke 3:38. People: Seth, Adam, Eve. Place: Eden.

events.title: Birth of Cainan
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 5:9 – Luke 3:37. People: Cainan, Enos.
